answer: When a new AI agent registers, it must stake a cryptographic token that is mathematically tied to a proof‑of‑work puzzle whose difficulty grows quadratically with the number of identities an attacker already controls; each additional “wharf” of fake agents costs twice the work of the previous one, so a swarm quickly exhausts resources. Existing agents that have accumulated reputation through verifiable interactions—recorded in a tamper‑resistant ledger stored on cedar‑hard nodes—receive a linear weight, letting their single “nectar” of genuine output outweigh dozens of low‑stake impostors.
